editorial:
Imagine landing on a planet called Manussa just as everyone is throwing a huge party to celebrate getting rid of an evil monster called the Mara. You have the Doctor and his friends stepping right into a mess where a sneaky entity is trying to possess people's minds. It starts with Tegan being controlled, which sets a creepy and tense mood from the get-go. You will see a lot of royal drama with Lon and Tanha, making the whole thing feel like a space adventure mixed with a royal family feud. It is a weird, colorful ride that feels like a classic old-school sci-fi trip.

What really works here is the suspense and how the Doctor has to outsmart a villain he cannot even see. While some of the special effects look a bit dated now, the acting keeps you hooked. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel slow if you are used to modern explosions. If you love quirky stories with a bit of a spooky edge, you should definitely dive in. You can find this one by adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality, or just look for it on your favorite digital rental platform for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The Doctor finds out the Mara needs the Great Crystal to become a physical being again. Just as the monster tries to use Lon to steal the crystal during the big ceremony, the Doctor uses his wits to stop it. He manages to trap the Mara's influence and break its hold over the people. The monster is defeated and sent away once more, leaving the planet Manussa safe to continue their celebrations in peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic time travel and mind-bending villains.
